name: Aave V3
description: The largest multi-chain lending market: supply assets to earn variable interest (receive aTokens), borrow against collateral at variable rates, use e-mode for correlated assets, flash-loan, and use GHO (Aave's stablecoin), Savings GHO (sGHO), AAVE staking and Umbrella aToken staking. Agents call the Pool (or the WrappedTokenGateway for native ETH/POL/AVAX/BNB) and read positions via the data providers or the public Aave V3 GraphQL API.

keyFunctions.description: Supply an asset: (asset, amount, onBehalfOf, referralCode=0). Amount in the asset's base units. ERC-20 approve(Pool, amount) first. Mints aTokens 1:1 to onBehalfOf; aToken balance grows with interest. Reverts if the reserve is paused, frozen, inactive or the supply cap is reached.

Withdraw supplied asset: (asset, amount, to). Burns aTokens. amount = type(uint256).max withdraws the whole balance. Reverts if it would push the health factor below 1 or if the reserve lacks liquidity (high utilisation). Returns the amount withdrawn.

Borrow: (asset, amount, interestRateMode, referralCode=0, onBehalfOf). interestRateMode must be 2 (variable); stable rate was removed in v3.2. Needs enough collateral (see getUserAccountData.availableBorrowsBase). Debt is a VariableDebtToken balance. Borrowing on behalf of another address needs credit delegation (approveDelegation on the variable debt token).

Repay debt: (asset, amount, interestRateMode=2, onBehalfOf). ERC-20 approve(Pool) first. amount = type(uint256).max repays the full debt of msg.sender (only when onBehalfOf = msg.sender; for others pass the exact amount). Returns the amount repaid.
Repay debt by burning your aTokens of the same asset: (asset, amount, interestRateMode=2). No approval needed. type(uint256).max repays up to the debt with available aTokens.
Enable/disable a supplied asset as collateral. Disabling reverts if it would drop the health factor below 1. Some assets (LTV 0 or isolated) cannot be enabled together with others.

Enter an efficiency-mode category (e.g. ETH-correlated or stablecoin) for higher LTV/liquidation threshold among correlated assets; 0 = leave e-mode. Reverts if current positions are not allowed in the category or the HF would fall below 1. Read categories with getEModeCategoryData / UiPoolDataProvider.getEModes.

Returns (totalCollateralBase, totalDebtBase, availableBorrowsBase, currentLiquidationThreshold, ltv, healthFactor). Base amounts are in the oracle base currency (USD with 8 decimals on these markets; check Oracle.BASE_CURRENCY_UNIT). ltv/threshold in bps. healthFactor has 18 decimals; below 1e18 the position can be liquidated; type(uint256).max when there is no debt.

Reserve state and config for an asset (ReserveDataLegacy struct): configuration bitmap, liquidityIndex, currentLiquidityRate and currentVariableBorrowRate (ray, 27 decimals, per-second-compounded APR), id, aTokenAddress, variableDebtTokenAddress, interestRateStrategyAddress, accruedToTreasury. Use it to find the aToken / debt token for an asset.
All reserve (underlying asset) addresses listed in this market.
E-mode category id the user is in (0 = none).
E-mode category LTV, liquidation threshold, liquidation bonus and label (legacy struct).

Flash loan one asset: (receiverAddress, asset, amount, params, referralCode). receiverAddress must be a contract implementing executeOperation and approve amount + premium back to the Pool in the same tx. Premium is FLASHLOAN_PREMIUM_TOTAL (governance-set, read it on the Pool).

Liquidate a position with health factor < 1: (collateralAsset, debtAsset, borrower, debtToCover, receiveAToken). Approve debtAsset first. Receives collateral plus the liquidation bonus. Usually up to 50% of the debt per call (100% when HF is very low or position small).
Current Pool proxy address of this market. Use it instead of hard-coding if in doubt.
Current AaveOracle address.
Current AaveProtocolDataProvider address.
ACLManager (roles: pool admin, emergency admin, risk admin).
(aTokenAddress, stableDebtTokenAddress [deprecated, zero/unused], variableDebtTokenAddress) for an underlying asset. The way to find an asset's aToken and debt token.
List of (symbol, tokenAddress) for every reserve in the market.
List of (symbol, aTokenAddress) for every aToken in the market.

(asset, user) -> currentATokenBalance, currentStableDebt (deprecated), currentVariableDebt, principalStableDebt, scaledVariableDebt, stableBorrowRate, liquidityRate, stableRateLastUpdated, usageAsCollateralEnabled. Balances in asset base units; rates in ray.

(decimals, ltv, liquidationThreshold, liquidationBonus, reserveFactor, usageAsCollateralEnabled, borrowingEnabled, stableBorrowRateEnabled, isActive, isFrozen). ltv/threshold/bonus in bps (bonus 10500 = 5%).
(borrowCap, supplyCap) in whole tokens (not base units); 0 = no cap.
True if the reserve is paused (no supply, withdraw, borrow, repay or liquidation).
Totals and rates: unbacked, accruedToTreasuryScaled, totalAToken, totalStableDebt, totalVariableDebt, liquidityRate, variableBorrowRate (ray), indexes, lastUpdateTimestamp.
Argument: the market's PoolAddressesProvider. Returns every reserve with config, caps, rates, prices, e-mode info, plus base-currency info. One call for a full market snapshot.
(PoolAddressesProvider, user) -> per-reserve scaled aToken balance, collateral flag, scaled variable debt, plus the user's e-mode id.
Argument: PoolAddressesProvider. All e-mode categories with their LTV, liquidation threshold, bonus and collateral/borrowable bitmaps.
Argument: PoolAddressesProvider. Reserve asset list.

Supply native gas token (ETH/POL/AVAX/BNB) with msg.value: (pool [unused, kept for compatibility; pass the Pool address], onBehalfOf, referralCode=0). Wraps to WETH/WPOL/etc. and mints the aToken to onBehalfOf.
Withdraw native token: (pool [unused], amount, to). First approve the gateway to spend your aWETH (aToken of the wrapped native) for amount. type(uint256).max withdraws all.

Borrow native token: (pool [unused], amount, referralCode=0). First call approveDelegation(gateway, amount) on the wrapped-native VariableDebtToken (from getReserveData(WETH).variableDebtTokenAddress); interest rate mode is variable.
Repay native-token debt with msg.value: (pool [unused], amount, onBehalfOf). Send msg.value >= amount; excess is refunded. type(uint256).max repays the whole debt if msg.value covers it.
Price of an asset in the base currency (USD, 8 decimals on these markets; check BASE_CURRENCY_UNIT). This is the price Aave uses for health factor and liquidations.
Prices for several assets.
Unit of the base currency (1e8 for USD-based markets).
Price feed (usually a Chainlink aggregator or a CAPO adapter) used for an asset.

offchainApis.name: Aave V3 GraphQL API (AaveKit API)
offchainApis.use: Markets, reserves, rates and user positions across all Aave V3 chains, and transaction building: simple queries return a TransactionRequest (to, data, value, chainId); complex ones return an ExecutionPlan (ApprovalRequired first, then the tx; or InsufficientBalanceError). Also sGHO vault previews and deposit/redeem plans. The URL is also a GraphQL playground.

actions.name: supply
actions.description: Lend an ERC-20 and earn interest
actions.how: ERC-20 approve(Pool, amount); Pool.supply(asset, amount, onBehalfOf=you, 0). Native token: WrappedTokenGatewayV3.depositETH(Pool, you, 0) with msg.value.

actions.name: withdraw
actions.description: Take supplied assets back
actions.how: Pool.withdraw(asset, amount or type(uint256).max, to). Native: approve aWETH to the gateway, then gateway.withdrawETH(Pool, amount, to).

actions.name: borrow
actions.description: Borrow against collateral at a variable rate
actions.how: Make sure the supplied asset is collateral (setUserUseReserveAsCollateral(asset,true) if needed), check Pool.getUserAccountData(you).availableBorrowsBase, convert to token units with Oracle.getAssetPrice, then Pool.borrow(asset, amount, 2, 0, you). Keep the health factor well above 1e18.

actions.name: repay
actions.description: Repay a loan
actions.how: approve(Pool, amount); Pool.repay(asset, amount or type(uint256).max, 2, you). Or repayWithATokens(asset, amount, 2) to repay with your deposits of the same asset.

actions.name: find aToken / debt token addresses
actions.description: Get the aToken and variable debt token of any reserve
actions.how: AaveProtocolDataProvider.getReserveTokensAddresses(asset) or Pool.getReserveData(asset).aTokenAddress / variableDebtTokenAddress. List reserves with Pool.getReservesList(). Full lists are in the per-market address-book file (…Assets library).

actions.name: check health / risk
actions.description: Read a user's position
actions.how: Pool.getUserAccountData(user) (healthFactor 18 decimals; < 1e18 = liquidatable); per-asset detail via ProtocolDataProvider.getUserReserveData(asset,user) or UiPoolDataProvider.getUserReservesData(provider,user).

actions.name: e-mode
actions.description: Higher LTV for correlated assets
actions.how: Read categories via UiPoolDataProvider.getEModes(provider); Pool.setUserEMode(categoryId). 0 exits.

actions.name: save in GHO
actions.description: Earn the GHO savings rate
actions.how: approve(sGHO, amount) on GHO; sGHO.deposit(amount, you). Exit any time with sGHO.redeem(shares, you, you).

actions.name: stake in Umbrella
actions.description: Earn extra rewards by covering bad debt
actions.how: approve the StakeToken for its asset() (wrapped aToken or GHO); StakeToken.deposit(assets, you). To exit: cooldown(), wait 20 days, then redeem within the 2-day window.

actions.name: build tx via API
actions.description: Let Aave build the calldata
actions.how: POST a GraphQL query to https://api.v3.aave.com/graphql (supply/borrow/repay/withdraw queries) and sign the returned TransactionRequest / ExecutionPlan steps.

risks: Liquidation: if the health factor (getUserAccountData, 18 decimals) drops below 1, anyone can repay part of the debt and seize collateral plus that reserve's liquidation bonus (getReserveConfigurationData.liquidationBonus, e.g. 10500 = 5%). Prices come from AaveOracle (mostly Chainlink feeds, some with CAPO price caps for LSTs/stablecoins); oracle errors or delays can cause unexpected liquidations.

Variable rates only: stable-rate borrowing was removed (v3.2); interestRateMode must be 2. Rates jump sharply above each reserve's optimal utilisation, and at 100% utilisation suppliers cannot withdraw until borrowers repay or new supply arrives.

Reserves can be frozen (no new supply/borrow; repay/withdraw still work) or paused (nothing works, including liquidations) by governance or the Protocol Guardian; supply and borrow caps can make transactions revert. Check ProtocolDataProvider.getReserveConfigurationData (isFrozen) and getPaused before acting.

Isolation mode / siloed borrowing / e-mode restrict what a user can borrow alongside certain collateral. The aave-v3-origin main branch marks debt-ceiling isolation and siloed borrowing as deprecated in v3.7.0 in favour of isolated e-mode categories; which behaviour applies depends on the version deployed in each market, so read the reserve config rather than assuming.
aTokens and debt tokens are rebasing (balances grow every second); integrations that cache balances will be off. Debt tokens are non-transferable.

Pools, aTokens and most periphery are upgradeable proxies controlled by Aave Governance V3 (AAVE holders, with timelocked executors) plus a Protocol Guardian multisig that can pause/freeze; contract logic can change after a governance vote.

Umbrella stakers and legacy stkAAVE/stkABPT can be slashed to cover bad debt (Umbrella: per asset/network, 20-day cooldown then a 2-day window, slashable during cooldown). sGHO has no cooldown and no slashing.

GHO is minted by facilitators (Aave pools, GSMs, bridges) with rates and caps set by governance; it is a soft-pegged stablecoin and can trade off peg. Bridged GHO on Base/Arbitrum/Avalanche moves via Chainlink CCIP.

L2 markets (Base, Arbitrum, Optimism, Polygon, Avalanche) use the L2Pool variant, which also accepts the normal Pool function signatures; BNB, Base and Ethereum Prime have different addresses from the shared 0x794a... Pool used on Arbitrum/Optimism/Polygon/Avalanche.
notes: Every address comes from the official BGD Labs aave-address-book (github.com/bgd-labs/aave-address-book, autogenerated from on-chain governance state; the aave.com docs point to it as the address registry). 'Ethereum Prime' is the market the address book still names AaveV3EthereumLido (its GHO steward is called GHO_AAVE_PRIME_STEWARD). keyFunctions are listed once on the Ethereum Core contracts; all other markets' Pool, PoolAddressesProvider, PoolDataProvider, UiPoolDataProvider, Gateway and Oracle share the same interface. Not listed on purpose: individual aTokens, variable debt tokens, stata tokens and per-asset oracles (hundreds; get them with getReserveTokensAddresses / getReserveData or the …Assets library in each address-book file), PoolConfigurator/ACLManager/Collector/EmissionManager (admin only), UiIncentiveDataProvider and RewardsController (in the address book if you need incentives), swap adapters (ParaSwap/CoW, change often), GHO GSMs (GhoEthereum.sol: GSM_USDC 0x3A3868898305f04beC7FEa77BecFf04C13444112, GSM_USDT 0x882285E62656b9623AF136Ce3078c6BdCc33F5E3 - not added as contracts because their underlying asset could not be re-checked on-chain during research), stkABPT, UmbrellaBatchHelper (0xCe6Ced23118EDEb23054E06118a702797b13fc2F in UmbrellaEthereum.sol; signatures not verified here), and Aave V3 on the ~30 other chains DefiLlama lists (Gnosis, Scroll, Linea, Sonic, zkSync, Mantle, Metis, Celo, Soneium, Plasma, MegaETH, X Layer, Monad, Ethereum EtherFi/Horizon markets, etc.: see AaveV3<Chain>.sol files in the address book). Aave V4 is a separate protocol (api.v4.aave.com) and not covered. All addresses have contract code on their chain (eth_getCode checked for every Ethereum address and every Pool/provider/gateway/oracle/UiPoolDataProvider elsewhere). Signatures come from aave-dao/aave-v3-origin interfaces, bgd-labs/aave-stk-v1-5 (stkAAVE) and Sourcify (Umbrella StakeToken, sGHO implementations). AAVE token and stkAAVE/umbrella use 18 decimals.

name: Arrakis Modular
description: Arrakis Modular is Arrakis Finance's vault framework for actively managed concentrated liquidity (Uniswap v3/v4, PancakeSwap, Aerodrome, Valantis HOT). An agent can discover public vaults through the ArrakisMetaVaultFactory, quote and deposit token pairs into a public vault for ERC20 LP shares through the ArrakisPublicVaultRouter, withdraw by burning shares, and read vault holdings and manager settings. Most TVL sits in private (Arrakis Pro) vaults that only their owner's whitelisted depositors can use.

contracts.name: Arrakis Public LP USDC/WETH vault (ArrakisMetaVaultPublic, HOT AMM module)

keyFunctions.description: Total token0 and token1 held by the vault's position (all depositors). Your share = balanceOf(you)/totalSupply().
Same as totalUnderlying but valued at a given sqrtPriceX96.
(init0, init1): token amounts needed to open a position when the vault is empty (totalSupply == 0).
Vault token0.
Vault token1.
Total LP shares (18 decimals).
LP share balance (vault shares are ERC20 and transferable).
Active module (DEX integration) holding the liquidity; can be changed by the vault owner via setModule (timelocked for public vaults).
Manager contract allowed to rebalance (ArrakisStandardManager).
Vault owner. For this vault: a TimeLock (0xCFaD8B6981Da1c734352Bd31618040C23FE99117) administered by the Arrakis multisig.

Direct mint of an exact number of shares to receiver; returns (amount0, amount1) pulled. Prefer the ArrakisPublicVaultRouter (it computes amounts and enforces min/max). Direct calls have no slippage bounds.
Direct burn of shares, sending token0/token1 to receiver; returns (amount0, amount1). No min-out check: prefer router.removeLiquidity.

actions.name: find public vaults
actions.description: List every public vault on a chain
actions.how: ArrakisMetaVaultFactory.numOfPublicVaults() then publicVaults(0, n); for each vault read name(), token0(), token1(), totalUnderlying(), totalSupply(), module(). Verify any vault address you get elsewhere with factory.isPublicVault(addr).

actions.name: deposit into a public vault
actions.description: Add token0/token1 liquidity and receive vault LP shares
actions.how: 1) router.getMintAmounts(vault, max0, max1) -> (shares, amt0, amt1). 2) approve ArrakisPublicVaultRouter (0x72aa2C8e6B14F30131081401Fa999fC964A66041) for token0 and token1 (or sign Permit2). 3) router.addLiquidity((max0, max1, min0, min1, minShares, vault, receiver)); use wrapAndAddLiquidity with msg.value to pay the WETH side in ETH. Set min values from the quote minus slippage: the docs warn vault composition can change before execution.

actions.name: withdraw from a public vault
actions.description: Burn LP shares for the underlying tokens
actions.how: approve the router to spend your vault shares (the vault address is the share token), then router.removeLiquidity((burnAmount, amount0Min, amount1Min, vault, receiver)). Preview with vault.totalUnderlying() * burnAmount / vault.totalSupply().

actions.name: deposit into a private (Arrakis Pro) vault
actions.description: Only for the vault owner's team
actions.how: vault owner calls whitelistDepositors([depositor]) on the ArrakisMetaVaultPrivate; the depositor approves vault.module() for the tokens and calls deposit(amount0, amount1) (payable for native ETH). Withdraw with withdraw(proportion, receiver) (owner only). Vaults are created by Arrakis on request.

actions.name: check who controls a vault
actions.description: Read manager guardrails and ownership
actions.how: vault.owner() (public vaults: a timelock), vault.manager(), ArrakisStandardManager.vaultInfo(vault) for executor, oracle, maxDeviation, maxSlippagePIPS, cooldownPeriod and managerFeePIPS.

risks: Active management: the vault's executor (an Arrakis-run backend set in ArrakisStandardManager) rebalances the position. Losses from rebalancing, impermanent loss and price moves fall on depositors; guardrails are an oracle deviation limit, max slippage and a cooldown per vault.

The vault owner can whitelist and switch modules (setModule), which changes where and how liquidity is deployed. For public vaults this is behind a timelock; for the Ethereum USDC/WETH vault the owner is TimeLock 0xCFaD8B6981Da1c734352Bd31618040C23FE99117 administered by the Arrakis multisig 0x5108EF86cF493905BcD35A3736e4B46DeCD7de58.

ArrakisStandardManager is an upgradeable (transparent) proxy whose admin is the Arrakis TimeLock 0xAf6f9640092cB1236E5DB6E517576355b6C40b7f; module implementations sit behind upgradeable beacons. Docs state all upgrades are timelocked and the Guardian can pause.

Public vs private: router functions only accept public vaults (onlyPublicVault). Private (Arrakis Pro) vaults are owned by a team through a PrivateVaultNFT; only whitelisted depositors can deposit and only the owner can withdraw. Anyone holding the NFT controls the funds.
Manager fee: a managerFeePIPS cut of earned swap fees (1% for the Ethereum USDC/WETH vault per docs).
The Ethereum USDC/WETH public vault uses the Valantis HOT AMM module, which relies on Arrakis-signed quotes (QuoteSigner) and Chainlink oracles.

Audits listed by Arrakis: ChainSecurity (Modular core Jul 2024, Uniswap V4 modules Dec 2024, Aerodrome Jan 2025), Sherlock, Watchpug, Enigma Dark, Cantina and Pashov (2023-2026). Reports are available on request from Arrakis; audits do not remove risk.
Public vault liquidity is small: on 2026-11-25 there were 2 public vaults on Ethereum, 6 on Base (mostly KAITO pairs), 1 on Arbitrum and none on Plasma or BNB Chain.
notes: Addresses come from the official arrakis-docs GitHub repo (deployments.md, last commit 2026-05-21). The public docs site docs.arrakis.finance was rebuilt in 2026 around 'Arrakis Pro' and no longer has the technical pages (old URLs such as /text/arrakisModular/deployments.html now redirect to /arrakis-pro); app.arrakis.finance returns 404, and the arrakis-modular source repo is not public. The core contracts are deployed with CREATE3 at the same address on every chain listed by Arrakis (Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, BNB Chain, Plasma, Optimism, Polygon, Ink, Unichain, Sepolia). Checked onchain 2026-11-25: the factory has code on Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, Plasma and BNB Chain, and the manager is the factory's manager() everywhere; the ArrakisPublicVaultRouter, RouterSwapExecutor (0x19488620Cdf3Ff1B0784AC4529Fb5c5AbAceb1B6) and RouterSwapResolver (0xC6c53369c36D6b4f4A6c195441Fe2d33149FB265) have NO code on Plasma or BNB Chain, so on those chains only private vaults exist. Other core addresses from the same page (not listed as contracts because agents rarely call them): PrivateVaultNFT 0x44A801e7E2E073bd8bcE4bCCf653239Fa156B762, RenderController 0x1Cc0Adff599F244f036a5C2425f646Aef884149D, TimeLock 0xAf6f9640092cB1236E5DB6E517576355b6C40b7f, Guardian 0x6F441151B478E0d60588f221f1A35BcC3f7aB981, Public Module Registry 0x791d75F87a701C3F7dFfcEC1B6094dB22c779603, Private Module Registry 0xe278C1944BA3321C1079aBF94961E9fF1127A265, Pauser 0x700a1cdA1495C1B34c4962e9742A8A8832aAc03A, Withdraw Helper 0x3a2e9c26fBB53990BAFAec0342e38bd2a06f46d3, Migration Helper 0xd61407B9B63956CfB61341AAfeFbD7EDA1F9B962; per-chain Uniswap V3/V4, PancakeSwap and Aerodrome module beacons are on the same deployments page. The docs quickstart describes an 'ArrakisPublicVaultRouterV2' (same function names), but the deployments page lists only the router at 0x72aa…6041, which Sourcify verifies as ArrakisPublicVaultRouter (v1); no V2 address is published, so it is left out. Per-vault addresses are not listed except the Ethereum USDC/WETH flagship vault documented on the official public vault list; discover the rest with factory.publicVaults(). The address 0xf790870ccF6aE66DdC69f68e6d05d446f1a6ad83 also holds WETH/USDC public vaults on Base and Arbitrum (same CREATE3 address, different modules), but official docs only describe the Ethereum one. DefiLlama also lists Robinhood Chain; Arrakis's deployment list does not, so it is not covered. Arrakis publishes no public API or SDK for Modular; an official Uniswap v4 position-migration example is at github.com/ArrakisFinance/univ4-migration-example. Older Arrakis V1/V2 (PALM) vaults are separate products not covered here.

name: Bitflow
description: The main DEX on Stacks (Bitcoin L2). Agents can swap and LP through HODLMM (bin-based concentrated liquidity, DLMM), XYK constant-product pools and StableSwap pools, or get the best route across Bitflow and other Stacks DEXs from Bitflow's public Quote API, which returns ready-made contract-call parameters.

keyFunctions.signature: swap-x-for-y-simple-multi(pool-trait <dlmm-pool-trait>, x-token-trait <sip-010-trait>, y-token-trait <sip-010-trait>, x-amount uint, min-dy uint, deadline-time (optional uint))
keyFunctions.description: Swap x-amount of the pool's X token for Y in one DLMM pool, walking up to 319 bins. Token traits must be the pool's x-token/y-token (read pool get-pool). Reverts err u2003 if output < min-dy, err u2012 if stacks-block-time (unix seconds) > deadline. Returns (ok {in, out}). Add post-conditions (Deny mode) for the tokens sent.

keyFunctions.signature: swap-y-for-x-simple-multi(pool-trait <dlmm-pool-trait>, x-token-trait <sip-010-trait>, y-token-trait <sip-010-trait>, y-amount uint, min-dx uint, deadline-time (optional uint))
keyFunctions.description: Reverse direction: Y in, X out, same rules.

keyFunctions.signature: swap-x-for-y-simple-range-multi(pool-trait <dlmm-pool-trait>, x-token-trait <sip-010-trait>, y-token-trait <sip-010-trait>, x-amount uint, min-dy uint, max-steps uint, deadline-time (optional uint))
keyFunctions.description: Same as swap-x-for-y-simple-multi but caps the number of bins traversed at max-steps (1-319) to bound execution cost.

keyFunctions.signature: swap-y-for-x-simple-range-multi(pool-trait <dlmm-pool-trait>, x-token-trait <sip-010-trait>, y-token-trait <sip-010-trait>, y-amount uint, min-dx uint, max-steps uint, deadline-time (optional uint))
keyFunctions.description: Y-for-X with a max-steps cap.

keyFunctions.signature: swap-simple-multi(swaps (list 5 {pool-trait: <dlmm-pool-trait>, x-token-trait: <sip-010-trait>, y-token-trait: <sip-010-trait>, amount: uint, min-received: uint, x-for-y: bool, max-steps: uint}), deadline-time (optional uint))
keyFunctions.description: Up to 5 single-pool swaps in one call (the form the Quote API returns as function_name swap-simple-multi; total max-steps should stay <= ~290 per docs). Each entry has its own min-received. Returns (ok {results: list of {in, out}}).

keyFunctions.signature: swap-multi(swaps (list 319 {pool-trait: <dlmm-pool-trait>, x-token-trait: <sip-010-trait>, y-token-trait: <sip-010-trait>, expected-bin-id: int, amount: uint, min-received: uint, x-for-y: bool}), max-unfavorable-bins uint, deadline-time (optional uint))
keyFunctions.description: Strict per-bin swap: each entry swaps in a specific expected-bin-id (signed, -500..500); fails with err u2002 if more than max-unfavorable-bins bins moved against you. Use the Quote API's 'full' parameters to build it.

keyFunctions.signature: add-relative-liquidity-same-multi(positions (list 288 {active-bin-id-offset: int, x-amount: uint, y-amount: uint, min-dlp: uint, max-x-liquidity-fee: uint, max-y-liquidity-fee: uint}), pool-trait <dlmm-pool-trait>, x-token-trait <sip-010-trait>, y-token-trait <sip-010-trait>, active-bin-tolerance (optional {expected-bin-id: int, max-deviation: uint}), deadline-time (optional uint))
keyFunctions.description: 'Simple mode' add: deposit into bins at offsets from the active bin at execution time. Only Y may go below the active bin, only X above it. min-dlp = minimum bin shares per position; max-*-liquidity-fee cap the fee charged for adding to the active bin. Optional tolerance reverts if the active bin moved more than max-deviation from expected-bin-id. Returns (ok {results, active-bin-id, active-bin-id-delta}). Broadcast in Allow mode per docs.

keyFunctions.signature: add-liquidity-multi(positions (list 333 {pool-trait: <dlmm-pool-trait>, x-token-trait: <sip-010-trait>, y-token-trait: <sip-010-trait>, bin-id: int, x-amount: uint, y-amount: uint, min-dlp: uint, max-x-liquidity-fee: uint, max-y-liquidity-fee: uint}), deadline-time (optional uint))
keyFunctions.description: 'Strict mode' add to exact bins. bin-id is SIGNED (-500..500) here; the API's prepare helpers output unsigned ids (0..1000) and the official executing code converts back (signed = unsigned - 500). Reverts if state changed. Returns (ok list of shares minted).

keyFunctions.signature: withdraw-liquidity-same-multi(positions (list 326 {pool-trait: <dlmm-pool-trait>, bin-id: int, amount: uint, min-x-amount: uint, min-y-amount: uint}), x-token-trait <sip-010-trait>, y-token-trait <sip-010-trait>, min-x-amount-total uint, min-y-amount-total uint, deadline-time (optional uint))
keyFunctions.description: Burn `amount` bin shares from each signed bin-id of one pool; totals are checked against min-x/y-amount-total. Size from the API's current-bins endpoint (userShares). Returns (ok {results, x-amount, y-amount}).

keyFunctions.signature: withdraw-relative-liquidity-same-multi(positions (list 300 {pool-trait: <dlmm-pool-trait>, active-bin-id-offset: int, amount: uint, min-x-amount: uint, min-y-amount: uint}), x-token-trait <sip-010-trait>, y-token-trait <sip-010-trait>, min-x-amount-total uint, min-y-amount-total uint, deadline-time (optional uint))
keyFunctions.description: Simple-mode withdraw by offset from the active bin.

keyFunctions.signature: withdraw-liquidity-multi(positions (list 326 {pool-trait: <dlmm-pool-trait>, x-token-trait: <sip-010-trait>, y-token-trait: <sip-010-trait>, bin-id: int, amount: uint, min-x-amount: uint, min-y-amount: uint}), deadline-time (optional uint))
keyFunctions.description: Withdraw across several pools/bins (per-position minimums).

keyFunctions.signature: move-liquidity-multi(positions (list 220 {pool-trait: <dlmm-pool-trait>, x-token-trait: <sip-010-trait>, y-token-trait: <sip-010-trait>, from-bin-id: int, to-bin-id: int, amount: uint, min-dlp: uint, max-x-liquidity-fee: uint, max-y-liquidity-fee: uint}), deadline-time (optional uint))
keyFunctions.description: Move `amount` shares from one bin to another (rebalancing a range) without leaving the pool.

keyFunctions.signature: move-relative-liquidity-multi(positions (list 208 {pool-trait: <dlmm-pool-trait>, x-token-trait: <sip-010-trait>, y-token-trait: <sip-010-trait>, from-bin-id: int, active-bin-id-offset: int, amount: uint, min-dlp: uint, max-x-liquidity-fee: uint, max-y-liquidity-fee: uint}), deadline-time (optional uint))
keyFunctions.description: Move shares to a bin at an offset from the active bin.

Full pool state: x-token (sBTC), y-token (USDCx), bin-step, active-bin-id (signed), protocol/provider/variable fees per side, core-address, pool status data. Other HODLMM pools (list via GET /quotes/v2/pools) expose the same interface.
Active bin, signed int (-500..500).
{x-balance, y-balance, bin-shares} for a bin. NOTE: this map is keyed by UNSIGNED id (signed + 500).

Quote Y out for x-amount of X (fees included). Declared public (takes traits) but makes no writes, so call it read-only via the Hiro call-read endpoint. Returns err u1010 if the pool is disabled.
Quote X out for y-amount of Y.
LP preview for adding x-amount: {dlp, y-amount required}.

keyFunctions.signature: swap-x-for-y(pool-trait <xyk-pool-trait>, x-token-trait <sip-010-trait>, y-token-trait <sip-010-trait>, x-amount uint, min-dy uint)
keyFunctions.description: Swap X for Y in an XYK v1.2 pool (pool contracts named xyk-pool-*-v-1-2 etc. under SM1793C4R5PZ4NS4VQ4WMP7SKKYVH8JZEWSZ9HCCR; get the list from get-pool-by-id or the Quote API). keyFunctions.signature: swap-y-for-x(pool-trait <xyk-pool-trait>, x-token-trait <sip-010-trait>, y-token-trait <sip-010-trait>, y-amount uint, min-dx uint)
keyFunctions.description: Swap Y for X; min-dx > 0.

keyFunctions.signature: add-liquidity(pool-trait <xyk-pool-trait>, x-token-trait <sip-010-trait>, y-token-trait <sip-010-trait>, x-amount uint, min-dlp uint)
keyFunctions.description: Add liquidity proportional to reserves: you supply x-amount and the contract pulls y-amount = x-amount * y-balance / x-balance. min-dlp (> 0) is the minimum LP tokens (the pool contract is the LP token). Returns (ok dlp).

keyFunctions.signature: withdraw-liquidity(pool-trait <xyk-pool-trait>, x-token-trait <sip-010-trait>, y-token-trait <sip-010-trait>, amount uint, min-x-amount uint, min-y-amount uint)
keyFunctions.description: Burn `amount` LP tokens for both tokens. Returns (ok {x-amount, y-amount}).
{id, name, symbol, pool-contract} for pool id 1..get-last-pool-id() (45 at research time).
Number of XYK v1.2 pools created.

offchainApis.use: GET /quotes/v2/pools, /quotes/v2/tokens, /quotes/v2/bins/{pool_id}; POST /quotes/v2/quote (best route incl. other Stacks DEXs) then /quotes/v2/swap or /quotes/v2/agg/swap for contract_address, function_name, args and Deny-mode post-conditions; GET /app/v2/users/{user}/positions/{pool_id}/current-bins to size LP withdrawals. Check /quotes/v2/status tip_lag == 0 first. 100 req/s per IP without a key.

offchainApis.use: 24h prices, volumes and USD liquidity per pair.

offchainApis.name: Bitflow SDK (@bitflowlabs/core-sdk)
offchainApis.use: TypeScript SDK for token lists, routes, quotes and swap execution; API keys optional (500 req/min per IP default).

actions.name: swap (best route)
actions.description: Swap any supported token pair at the best price across Bitflow and other Stacks venues.
actions.how: POST /quotes/v2/quote {input_token, output_token, amount_in (base units, string), slippage_tolerance}; take an executable route; POST /quotes/v2/swap (or /quotes/v2/agg/swap for agg_buildable routes); sign a Stacks contract-call with the returned contract, function, args and post-conditions (Deny mode).

actions.name: swap in one HODLMM pool
actions.description: Direct DLMM swap.
actions.how: Read pool get-pool for x-token/y-token; dlmm-swap-router-v-1-2.swap-x-for-y-simple-multi(pool, x-token, y-token, amount, min-out, (some deadline)) with post-conditions on the token sent.

actions.name: swap in an XYK pool
actions.description: Constant-product swap.
actions.how: xyk-core-v-1-2.get-dy(pool, x, y, amount) read-only; then swap-x-for-y(pool, x, y, amount, quote*(1-slippage)). Use token-stx-v-1-2 for STX.

actions.name: add HODLMM liquidity
actions.description: Provide liquidity in bins around the price.
actions.how: Get bins from /quotes/v2/bins/{pool}; build positions (Y below active bin, X above); dlmm-liquidity-router-v-1-2.add-relative-liquidity-same-multi(positions, pool, x, y, (some {expected-bin-id, max-deviation}), deadline).

actions.name: remove HODLMM liquidity
actions.description: Withdraw bin shares.
actions.how: GET /app/v2/users/{you}/positions/{pool}/current-bins (require clean, complete, tipLag 0); withdraw-liquidity-same-multi with signed bin ids (unsigned - 500) and per-bin share amounts.

risks: Admin powers: XYK/StableSwap core admins (up to 5 principals) can disable pools (set-pool-status), change protocol/provider fees and fee addresses; the swap helper has an on/off switch; HODLMM pools have variable-fee managers and are administered via the DLMM core. A disabled pool makes swaps revert (e.g. legacy xyk-pool-stx-aeusdc-v-1-1/v-1-2 returned err u1010 POOL_DISABLED at research time).
Contracts are versioned, not upgradeable: new versions (v-1-1 -> v-1-2) replace old ones, so integrations must follow current addresses; old pools may be disabled or drained of liquidity.

Audits listed in docs: Clarity Alliance (XYK June 2024, StableSwap Sept 2024, StableSwap staking Sept 2024, StableSwap Midpoint Mar/Apr 2025), CoinFabrik (Dec 2023), StrataLabs (June 2023). No HODLMM/DLMM audit is listed on the docs audits page. Immunefi bug bounty is live.

HODLMM quotes and position data come from an off-chain engine that can lag the chain (check tip_lag); strict-mode transactions revert if the active bin moves, simple-mode ones execute at the then-current bin.

Stacks transactions should use Deny-mode post-conditions; without them a malicious token trait could move more funds than expected. Only pass token/pool traits that match the pool's own x-token/y-token.
Many listed tokens are bridged (sBTC, aeUSDC, USDCx, pBTC etc.) and carry their bridge's risk.
notes: Stacks is a Clarity-VM chain, so vm is 'mixed', chainId is null and addresses are contract principals. Signatures are Clarity (name(arg type, ...)); trait arguments are passed as contract principals. Sources: the DLMM swap/liquidity routers are named in the official HODLMM API docs (v1 page), the sBTC/USDCx pool in the v2 docs, stableswap-stx-ststx-v-1-2 and xyk-core-v-1-1 on the docs 'Deployed Contracts > Stacks' page, and xyk-core-v-1-2, xyk-swap-helper-v-1-2, stableswap-core-v-1-2 and token-stx-v-1-2 in Bitflow's official npm SDK (@bitflowlabs/core-sdk 4.2.0, dist/src/keeper/types.js ALLOWED_CONTRACTS, and pool data) — the docs deployed-contracts page has not been updated for these v1.2 contracts, but they are the active ones (xyk-core-v-1-2 ~144k txs vs v1.1 ~10k). Every contract was confirmed via the Hiro API (interface/source) on 2026-11-25 and signatures were taken from the deployed Clarity source. Left out: dlmm-core-v-1-1 (the routers call SP1PFR4V08H1RAZXREBGFFQ59WB739XM8VVGTFSEA.dlmm-core-v-1-1, but that address is not listed on any official page I could find), Bitflow's agg-* aggregator routers (only agg-treasury-v-1-1 is named in docs; the Quote API returns the router to call), the other legacy StableSwap pairs/earn/LP-token contracts and the old cross-DEX routers/wrappers on the deployed-contracts page (still listed there; see that page), keeper contracts, and individual pool contracts beyond one HODLMM example (discover pools via GET /quotes/v2/pools or core get-pool-by-id).

name: Chainlink
description: Oracle network. Agents read Chainlink Data Feeds (AggregatorV3 proxy contracts, e.g. ETH/USD) on-chain for reference prices, and move tokens or messages between chains with CCIP by calling the CCIP Router (getFee, then ccipSend). LINK is the network's ERC-677 token and a CCIP fee token.

keyFunctions.description: Returns (uint80 roundId, int256 answer, uint256 startedAt, uint256 updatedAt, uint80 answeredInRound). answer is the ETH / USD price scaled by 10^decimals() (8 here). Heartbeat for this feed is 3600 s and deviation threshold 0.5% (per Chainlink's feed directory): the answer updates when price moves more than 0.5% or 3600 s pass. Reject the answer if block.timestamp - updatedAt > heartbeat (plus a small buffer), if answer <= 0, or if updatedAt == 0.
Number of decimals in answer (8 for this feed). Always read it rather than hard-coding; some Chainlink feeds use 18.
Human-readable pair, returns "ETH / USD". Use it to sanity-check you have the right proxy.
Same tuple as latestRoundData for a historical roundId (round ids are phase-encoded; not guaranteed contiguous across aggregator upgrades).
Current underlying aggregator behind this proxy. Always read prices from the proxy, never the aggregator, since Chainlink swaps aggregators behind the proxy.

offchainApis.name: Data Feeds directory (data.chain.link)
offchainApis.use: Search every Chainlink feed by pair and network; each feed page shows the proxy address to call, decimals, heartbeat and deviation threshold, and whether it is deprecated.

offchainApis.name: Feed reference data directory (JSON)
offchainApis.use: Machine-readable list of all feeds for one network (the same data docs.chain.link renders). Fields: name, proxyAddress (call this), decimals, heartbeat, threshold, feedCategory, docs.hidden / shutdownDate. {network} examples: mainnet (Ethereum), ethereum-mainnet-base-1, ethereum-mainnet-arbitrum-1, ethereum-mainnet-optimism-1, matic-mainnet, bsc-mainnet, avalanche-mainnet. Some entries have secondaryProxyAddress/secondaryProxyEns (e.g. Base ETH/USD): the standard proxy is the one whose ens is the plain pair name (eth-usd); 'svr' proxies are Smart Value Recapture variants.

offchainApis.name: CCIP Directory
offchainApis.use: Per-chain Router address, chain selector, fee tokens, supported lanes and supported tokens (with token pool and rate limits) for CCIP mainnet.

offchainApis.name: CCIP Explorer
offchainApis.use: Track a CCIP message by messageId or source tx hash (status: waiting for finality, committed, success/failure; manual execution if it failed on the destination).

actions.name: read-price
actions.description: Get a reference USD price on-chain
actions.how: Call latestRoundData() on the feed proxy for the pair and chain (this file for ETH/BTC/USDC; any other pair: look up the proxyAddress on data.chain.link or the reference-data-directory JSON). price = answer / 10^decimals(). Reject if answer <= 0 or now - updatedAt > heartbeat. On Arbitrum/Base/Optimism first check the L2 Sequencer Uptime Feed (answer == 0 and now - startedAt > grace period).

actions.name: ccip-token-transfer
actions.description: Bridge a CCIP-supported token to another chain
actions.how: 1) Confirm the token is supported on the lane in the CCIP Directory and router.isChainSupported(destSelector). 2) token.approve(router, amount). 3) Build EVM2AnyMessage{receiver: abi.encode(recipient), data: "", tokenAmounts: [(token, amount)], feeToken: LINK or address(0), extraArgs: 0x181dcf10 ++ abi.encode(0, true)}. 4) fee = router.getFee(destSelector, msg). 5) If feeToken is LINK, LINK.approve(router, fee) (plus amount if LINK is also the token sent); else send value = fee. 6) router.ccipSend(destSelector, msg). 7) Track messageId on ccip.chain.link.

actions.name: ccip-message
actions.description: Send arbitrary data to a receiver contract on another chain
actions.how: Same as token transfer with data = your payload, tokenAmounts = [], and extraArgs gasLimit sized for the receiver's ccipReceive (the receiver must implement CCIPReceiver / IAny2EVMMessageReceiver).

actions.name: get-link
actions.description: Obtain/identify official LINK
actions.how: Use the LINK address for the chain from this file (from docs.chain.link/resources/link-token-contracts). On BNB Chain and Polygon, bridged LINK from the chain's native bridge is not ERC-677 and must be converted with Chainlink PegSwap before use with Chainlink services.

risks: Stale prices: a feed only updates on its deviation threshold or heartbeat; always compare updatedAt with the heartbeat listed for that feed, and do not assume the same heartbeat across chains (e.g. ETH/USD is 3600 s on Ethereum but 27 s on Polygon, 86400 s on Avalanche).

Feeds get deprecated: Chainlink marks feeds for shutdown on data.chain.link and in the directory JSON (shutdownDate / hidden). A deprecated proxy can stop updating; check before integrating and re-check periodically.

Use the proxy, never the aggregator address; aggregators are replaced during upgrades. Several networks also list SVR (Smart Value Recapture) proxies and Arbitrum lists hidden 'cre-backup' proxies for the same pair with different decimals (18): read decimals() and use the standard proxy unless you specifically want SVR.

L2s (Arbitrum, Base, Optimism): if the sequencer is down, feeds can look fresh but be wrong for users who cannot transact; check the L2 Sequencer Uptime Feed and enforce a grace period after it comes back up. The directory JSON currently flags the Optimism sequencer feed as hidden although the L2 sequencer docs page still lists it.

Data feeds are market references with a deviation band (e.g. 0.5%); they are not exact execution prices and can be manipulated on low-liquidity assets ('medium'/'high' risk categories on data.chain.link).

CCIP fees: getFee depends on the destination, data size, gas limit and token amounts; overpaid native fees are not refunded. Messages wait for source-chain finality (minutes on Ethereum, can be longer on some chains).

CCIP rate limits: each token pool has per-lane capacity and refill-rate limits; transfers above the available capacity revert. Check the token's rate limits in the CCIP Directory before large transfers.

CCIP chain selectors are not EVM chain IDs; sending to a wrong selector or an unsupported lane reverts with UnsupportedDestinationChain. Receiver must be abi.encode(address) for EVM destinations; tokens sent to a contract that cannot handle them may be stuck.
Bridged LINK from BNB Chain's and Polygon's native bridges is not ERC-677 and is not usable with Chainlink services; use PegSwap to convert. LINK on Avalanche reports symbol LINK.e.
notes: DefiLlama lists Chainlink as a parent protocol 'chainlink' with child entries (Chainlink Requests 'chainlink-requests', CCIP, Chainlink Staking); 'chainlink' is used because this file covers Data Feeds, CCIP and LINK together. Feed proxies are the standard (non-SVR) proxies from Chainlink's reference data directory JSON, which docs.chain.link/data-feeds/price-feeds/addresses loads; on Base the standard eth-usd and btc-usd proxies appear as secondaryProxyAddress of the shared-SVR entries. LINK/USD is included for Ethereum only. All feeds were checked on 2026-11-25 with description(), decimals() (all 8) and latestRoundData() (ETH ~1652 USD, BTC ~58,950 USD, USDC ~0.9999 USD); all CCIP routers returned typeAndVersion 'Router 1.2.0' and isChainSupported true for the other test chains; all LINK addresses returned decimals 18. Left out: the Ethereum Feed Registry: docs.chain.link/data-feeds/feed-registry now redirects to the Data Feeds overview and no current official page lists its address, so it is omitted (read individual proxies instead). Other CCIP contracts per chain (RMN proxy/armProxy, TokenAdminRegistry, RegistryModuleOwnerCustom, TokenPoolFactory, OnRamps/OffRamps) are listed in the CCIP Directory and in https://github.com/smartcontractkit/documentation/blob/main/src/config/data/ccip/v1_2_0/mainnet/chains.json. Every other price feed (thousands, on 50+ networks) is listed at data.chain.link with its proxy address. Polygon here means Polygon PoS (chainId 137).

offchainApis.name: CCTP attestation API (Iris) - mainnet
offchainApis.use: GET /v2/messages/{sourceDomainId}?transactionHash=0x... returns the message and attestation for a burn (poll until status complete), then pass both to MessageTransmitterV2.receiveMessage on the destination. Also GET /v2/burn/USDC/fees/{sourceDomainId}/{destDomainId} (fees for maxFee), GET /v2/fastBurn/USDC/allowance (Fast Transfer allowance), POST /v2/quote/burn/usdc/{sourceDomainId}/{destDomainId} (fee quote), POST /v2/reattest/{nonce}, GET /v2/publicKeys; legacy GET /v1/attestations/{messageHash} and /v1/messages/{sourceDomainId}/{transactionHash}. Rate limit 40 requests/second; exceeding it blocks all requests for 5 minutes (HTTP 429).

offchainApis.use: Same endpoints for testnets.

actions.name: bridge-usdc
actions.description: Move native USDC to another chain with CCTP V2
actions.how: 1) USDC.approve(TokenMessengerV2, amount); 2) TokenMessengerV2.depositForBurn(amount, destDomain, bytes32(recipient), USDC, bytes32(0), maxFee, 1000 fast | 2000 standard) with maxFee from GET /v2/burn/USDC/fees/{src}/{dst}; 3) poll GET https://iris-api.circle.com/v2/messages/{srcDomain}?transactionHash=<burn tx> until attestation is ready; 4) on destination call MessageTransmitterV2.receiveMessage(message, attestation)

actions.name: check-blacklist
actions.description: Check whether Circle has frozen an address
actions.how: contract USDC.isBlacklisted(address) on EVM chains

risks: Centralised issuer: the FiatToken blacklister role can blacklist any address; a blacklisted address cannot call transfer/transferFrom and cannot receive tokens (stablecoin-evm token design doc).
The pauser role can pause the whole token, blocking all transfers, mints and burns.
EVM USDC/EURC are upgradeable (FiatTokenProxy, unstructured-storage proxy delegating to FiatToken); the admin role can switch the implementation.

CCTP: destinationDomain is Circle's domain ID (e.g. Ethereum 0, Avalanche 1, OP 2, Arbitrum 3, Solana 5, Base 6, Polygon 7, Unichain 10), not the EVM chain ID. A wrong mintRecipient encoding loses funds. $10M max per burn; Fast Transfers are limited by a global allowance and carry a fee.
CCTP V1 (Legacy) deprecation began October 31, 2026 and completes December 1, 2026; message limits tighten until no new burns are possible and contracts are paused. Use V2 for new transfers.
Bridged USDC (e.g. USDC.e) on some chains is not issued by Circle; only addresses on Circle's page are native USDC.
notes: Token addresses are copied from Circle's USDC and EURC contract-address pages (EVM addresses checksummed). CCTP V2 EVM addresses are identical on most chains (TokenMessengerV2 0x28b5a0e9C621a5BadaA536219b3a228C8168cf5d, MessageTransmitterV2 0x81D40F21F12A8F0E3252Bccb954D722d4c464B64) except EDGE. Also on the CCTP V2 page but not listed as contracts here: TokenMinterV2 (0xfd78EE919681417d192449715b2594ab58f5D002 on most chains), MessageV2 (0xec546b6B005471ECf012e5aF77FBeC07e0FD8f78) and TokenMessengerWithFees (0x71f54F818671cD0D7ea140Da213e5C8b5C92a408 on 18 chains) - see https://developers.circle.com/cctp/references/contract-addresses. CCTP on Starknet, Stellar, Sui, Aptos and Noble: see Circle's non-EVM references (not included). BNB Smart Chain is CCTP domain 17 for USYC only. EVM keyFunctions follow Circle's FiatToken (stablecoin-evm) design; verify with get_abi. chainId is null where Circle's page does not give it and it was not confirmed (Arc, Codex, EDGE, Pharos). proxy is null because per-address proxy status was not confirmed from Circle's pages, though FiatToken is designed to sit behind FiatTokenProxy.

name: Clanker
description: Clanker is a permissionless token launchpad (Farcaster bot, clanker.world, API and contracts). Clanker v5, the current version, launches fixed-supply ERC-20s into Uniswap v4 pools whose hook charges a 1-10% buy/sell tax that pays Clanker, the creator's reward recipients and optional holder dividends, burns and an integrator. An agent can launch tokens (partner API or factory.createLaunch), read pool tax terms, claim creator rewards from the FeeEscrow and claim holder dividends.

keyFunctions.description: Params: ((address creator,(address recipient,address admin,uint16 relativeWeightBps,bool isCreator)[] feeSlots,string tokenName,string tokenSymbol,string tokenContractURI,bytes32 creatorSalt,address quoteToken,uint64 expectedConfigVersion,uint64 deadline,bool metadataEditable,string[] metadataKeys,string[] metadataValues,(uint32 buyTaxRate,uint32 sellTaxRate,uint32 creatorAllocationShare,uint32 burnAllocationShare,uint32 dividendAllocationShare,uint32 integratorAllocationShare,uint256 minimumDividendHolding) taxConfiguration,address creatorFeeRecipient,address integratorFeeRecipient,bool antiSnipeEnabled)). Deploy a v5 token (fixed 1B supply, 18 decimals, no owner/minter) and its Uniswap v4 pool with all supply as locked single-sided liquidity. msg.value must equal nativeLaunchFee() (0 on 2026-11-25). Rules: expectedConfigVersion must equal configVersion() (else StaleConfig); up to 7 feeSlots whose relativeWeightBps sum to 10000; rates/shares use 1e8 = 100%; buy/sell tax within the policy (1%-10%); the four allocation shares sum to 1e8; quoteToken must be registered (quoteConfig); the predicted token address must end in 'cccc', so creatorSalt has to be mined (see launchTokenInitCodeHash). Most integrators use the Clanker API or clanker-sdk/v5 instead. Returns (token, poolId).

offchainApis.name: Clanker deploy API (partner)
offchainApis.use: POST a v5 launch: {protocol:'v5', chainId, token:{name, symbol, image, tokenAdmin, description, socialMediaUrls, requestKey}, tax:{buyFee, sellFee, dividends, minimumDividendHolding, burn, integrator, antiSnipeEnabled, metadataEditable}, pool:{pairedToken}, rewards:[{admin, recipient, allocation}], dryRun}. Header x-api-key: <partner key issued by the Clanker team>. Returns expectedAddress; deployment is queued. Limits: 20 launches/day and 1/minute per key (429 with Retry-After). dryRun:true validates without deploying. /api/tokens/deploy/v4 is gone (410).

offchainApis.name: Clanker public API
offchainApis.use: Token search/list (GET /api/tokens?q=&chainId=&includeMarket=), market data, trades, holders, GET /api/tokens/{address}/fees (tax config, fee history, claimed/unclaimed), GET /api/creator-earnings/{tokenAddress}?chainId= (unclaimed FeeEscrow balances of reward recipients), GET /api/metadata/factories (current v5 taxPolicy and launchCreationEnabled). Rate limited per IP.

offchainApis.name: Clanker authenticated API
offchainApis.use: Partner endpoints with header x-api-key: higher-limit token search (/api/tokens/authenticated), tokens by admin, is-blocked check, LP/claim info, POST /api/tokens/index to index a token deployed outside the API.

offchainApis.name: clanker-sdk (TypeScript)
offchainApis.use: npm install clanker-sdk viem; import { Clanker } from 'clanker-sdk/v5' to launch and manage v5 tokens onchain with your own wallet (handles salt mining and params); clanker-sdk/v4, /v3 and /legacyFeeClaims manage older tokens.

actions.name: launch a token (API)
actions.description: Deploy a v5 token without handling salts
actions.how: POST https://www.clanker.world/api/tokens/deploy with x-api-key (partner key) and the v5 body; try dryRun:true first. Returns expectedAddress.

actions.name: launch a token (onchain)
actions.description: Deploy from your own wallet
actions.how: Use clanker-sdk/v5, or call Factory.createLaunch(launchParams) with expectedConfigVersion = configVersion(), a registered quoteToken, rates in 1e8 units, feeSlot weights summing to 10000, a deadline, and a creatorSalt that makes the predicted address end in cccc; msg.value = nativeLaunchFee(). Simulate first. createLaunchAndBuy adds a creator buy.

actions.name: claim creator rewards
actions.description: Withdraw a reward recipient's tax share
actions.how: FeeEscrow.owed(recipient, currency) (currency = zero address for native ETH/BNB etc., or the pair stablecoin), then FeeEscrow.claimFor(recipient, currency) (anyone can trigger; pays the recipient) or claimTo(currency, destination) from the recipient wallet. One claim pays the balance of all that recipient's v5 tokens. Or the token's admin page https://www.clanker.world/clanker/<token>/admin.

actions.name: claim holder dividends
actions.description: Collect dividends of v5 tokens you hold
actions.how: Factory.dividendOf(token) -> dividend contract; read withdrawableDividendOf(holder); claim with withdrawDividendsFor(holder, unwrapWrappedNative) or DividendClaimHelper.claimDividends([(token, unwrap)...]) for up to 64 tokens.

actions.name: check a token before trading
actions.description: Confirm it is a real Clanker v5 token and see its tax
actions.how: Factory.isLaunchToken(token) on the right chain; Factory.creatorRights(token).poolId; Hook.poolConfig(poolId) and Hook.effectiveFeeRates(poolId, isBuy). Also GET /api/tokens?q=<address> for warning tags.

actions.name: trade a v5 token
actions.description: Buy or sell
actions.how: Swap in the token's Uniswap v4 pool (hooks = the chain's v5 Hook, tickSpacing 200 at launch) through the Uniswap Universal Router + Permit2 (see the uniswap registry entry). The hook takes the buy/sell tax from each swap; exact-output swaps revert during the sniper window.

risks: Anyone can launch a Clanker token; most are memecoins and many are scams, rugs-by-dumping or impersonations of real projects/people. A Clanker launch says nothing about the project. Check Factory.isLaunchToken and clanker.world warning tags (UNUSUAL_TICK, UNUSUAL_PAIR_ADDRESS, MISSING_POOL_CONFIG, UNUSUAL_POSITIONS); a token without tags is not safe.

v5 tokens charge a buy and sell tax of 1-10% each on every pool swap, plus a sniper fee that starts at 99% and decays to the normal tax over 20 seconds after launch (if enabled). Buying in the first seconds can lose almost everything to the fee.

Launch liquidity is the whole supply, placed by the hook as single-sided liquidity from the launch price, and can never be removed (no LP pull). The creator gets tokens only by buying (e.g. createLaunchAndBuy) and can sell like anyone else; early buyers dumping can take the price back toward the launch level.

Tax terms are frozen per pool at launch; the factory owner can change policy, quote tokens and pause launches only for new launches. v5 contracts are not upgradeable. The factory owner or creator admin can change dividend exclusions/receivers and emergency-withdraw assets held by any token's dividend contract.
Metadata (name, symbol, image) can be changed after launch by the creator if metadataEditable was set; do not rely on name/symbol to identify a token.
Reward and dividend balances are per recipient across all v5 tokens in the FeeEscrow, so a per-token figure from the API is an estimate.
Audits listed on the Clanker docs: v5 by XORS (November 2026); v4.1 Macro; v4.0 Cantina and Macro; v3.1 Macro; v2.0 Quantstamp. Audits do not make individual tokens safe.
notes: Clanker v5 is the current version per the official docs (Core Contracts page: 'Clanker v5 is the current version'); launched on Base on 2026-10-31 and on BNB Chain, Monad, Robinhood Chain, X Layer, Arc and Elysium on 2026-11-04/05. The deploy API only launches v5 (v4 launches are no longer available). Each factory exposes hook(), dividendDeployer(), announcementRegistry(), launchValidation(), launchBuyAdapter(), tokenDeployer(); checked onchain 2026-11-25 that every listed factory's hook() and hook.feeEscrow() match the docs and that all listed addresses have code. Elysium (Kinetiq chain, id 99901; Factory 0xcA111dcdd2cE924c3378d6514fDCbC46217bcA16, Hook 0x3eA9581a32a396F69b177B65b91149Cf887BEACC per docs) is not listed as contracts because it has no public RPC to confirm code. Supporting v5 contracts (Dividend Deployer, Launch Validation, Launch Operations, Launch Buy Adapter, Token Deployer, Dividend Implementation) are on the Deployed Contracts page; integrators do not call them. Base Announcement Registry is listed; on the other chains it is 0x2D75afC0Cdf502E4381dC0B23327BFeD358bA43A. Older versions keep working for their own tokens and are NOT listed as contracts: v4.0/v4.1 (Uniswap v4 LP-fee tokens; Base factory Clanker 0xE85A59c628F7d27878ACeB4bf3b35733630083a9, fees claimed from ClankerFeeLocker 0xF3622742b1E446D92e45E22923Ef11C2fcD55D68 via claim(feeOwner, token) / availableFees(feeOwner, token), LP locked in ClankerLpLockerFeeConversion 0x63D2DfEA64b3433F4071A98665bcD7Ca14d93496; v4 also on BNB Chain, Monad, Robinhood Chain and on the retired Ethereum, Arbitrum and Unichain deployments), v3.1, v3.0, v2.0, v1.0 and v0 (Base, Uniswap v3). All per-chain addresses for every version are on https://clanker.gitbook.io/documentation/references/deployed-contracts. Clanker no longer supports Ethereum, Arbitrum One and Unichain for new launches. DefiLlama lists Base only. The Clanker docs are also served to agents through a GitBook MCP server (https://clanker.gitbook.io/documentation/~gitbook/mcp). Function signatures are from Sourcify-verified sources (factory partial match, others exact match).

name: Compound V2
description: Legacy pooled money market on Ethereum (Comptroller + cTokens). As of late 2026 every V2 market has supply (mint) and borrow paused, so agents use it to read positions, redeem cTokens, repay or liquidate borrows and claim previously accrued COMP. New lending happens on Compound III (Comet).

keyFunctions.description: Mark the given cTokens as collateral (needed before borrowing against them). Returns one error code per market (0 = ok).
Stop using a cToken as collateral. Fails if the account still borrows from that market or exiting would leave it short.
Returns (error, liquidity, shortfall) in USD scaled 1e18. shortfall > 0 means the account can be liquidated.
(account, cTokenModify, redeemTokens, borrowAmount) -> (error, liquidity, shortfall) after a hypothetical redeem/borrow.
cTokens the account has entered as collateral.
Returns (isListed, collateralFactorMantissa (1e18 = 100%), isComped).
All listed cToken addresses.
True if minting in that cToken is paused (true for every market as of 2026-11-25).
True if borrowing in that cToken is paused (true for every market as of 2026-11-25).
True if the market is deprecated (collateral factor 0, borrow paused, reserve factor 100%): any borrow there can be fully liquidated.
Max share of a borrow repayable in one liquidation (0.5e18 = 50% on 2026-11-25).
Collateral bonus to liquidators, 1e18-scaled (1.08e18 = 8% on 2026-11-25).
(cTokenBorrowed, cTokenCollateral, repayAmount) -> (error, cTokens seized).
COMP already accrued but not yet claimed (excludes amounts since the last index update).
Claim accrued COMP for a holder across all markets (anyone may call; COMP goes to the holder). V2 COMP supply/borrow speeds are 0, so only past accruals remain.
Claim accrued COMP for a holder in the given markets only (cheaper).
Price oracle used by the Comptroller (currently the Compound v2 Price Feed).

contracts.name: cETH - Compound V2 market for ETH

keyFunctions.description: Supply ETH (msg.value) for cETH. Reverts on failure. Guardian-paused as of 2026-11-25.
Burn cETH (8 decimals) for ETH. Reverts on failure.
Withdraw an exact amount of ETH (wei).

actions.name: withdraw-supply
actions.description: Withdraw supplied assets from a V2 market
actions.how: cToken.redeemUnderlying(amount in underlying units) or cToken.redeem(cTokenAmount). Check Comptroller.getHypotheticalAccountLiquidity(account, cToken, redeemTokens, 0) if you also borrow, and cToken.getCash() for available liquidity. Check the uint return value: 0 = success.

actions.name: repay
actions.description: Repay a V2 borrow
actions.how: ERC-20 markets: underlying.approve(cToken, amt) then cToken.repayBorrow(amt) (2^256-1 = full). cETH: Maximillion.repayBehalf(borrower) with a little more ETH than borrowBalanceCurrent (excess refunded).

actions.name: check-health
actions.description: Read an account's position
actions.how: Comptroller.getAccountLiquidity(account) -> (err, liquidity, shortfall) in USD 1e18; per market cToken.getAccountSnapshot(account); collateral factors via Comptroller.markets(cToken).

actions.name: liquidate
actions.description: Liquidate an account with shortfall
actions.how: When getAccountLiquidity shows shortfall > 0: approve the borrowed underlying, then cTokenBorrowed.liquidateBorrow(borrower, repayAmount <= closeFactor x borrow, cTokenCollateral); you receive collateral cTokens, then redeem them.

actions.name: claim-comp
actions.description: Claim accrued COMP
actions.how: Comptroller.claimComp(holder) (or claimComp(holder, [cTokens])). Read Comptroller.compAccrued(holder) first; new COMP emissions on V2 are zero.

actions.name: exit-collateral
actions.description: Remove a market from collateral
actions.how: Comptroller.exitMarket(cToken) once nothing is borrowed from it and the account stays healthy.

risks: Legacy version: Compound V2 is being wound down; the current product is Compound III (Comet), which has separate per-base-asset deployments not covered here.

On-chain state checked 2026-11-25: mintGuardianPaused and borrowGuardianPaused are true for all 20 listed markets, so mint() and borrow() revert; redeem, repay and liquidation still work. COMP supply/borrow speeds are 0 on every market.
Deprecated markets (isDeprecated = true: cUSDT, cZRX, cCOMP, cTUSD, cUSDP, cFEI, cREP, cSAI) have collateral factor 0 and 100% reserve factor, so open borrows there can be liquidated in full.

Collateral factors on the remaining markets (e.g. cUSDC 84.5%, cDAI 83.5%, cETH 82.5% on 2026-11-25) can be cut by governance at any time, which can push accounts into shortfall; closeFactor is 50% and liquidation incentive 8%.
Liquidity risk: redeem fails if the market's getCash() is below the requested amount (cash is lent out to borrowers).
Many write functions return a non-zero error code instead of reverting (CErc20 mint/redeem/borrow/repay). Always check the return value or the Failure event; cETH reverts instead.
Oracle risk: prices come from the Compound v2 Price Feed (Chainlink feeds, configurable by the Compound community multisig); deprecated FEI, REP and SAI use fixed prices.
Governance: the Comptroller and all markets are administered by the Timelock controlled by COMP holders via GovernorBravo; parameters, pauses and implementations can change by vote.
Past incident (26 Nov 2020): a brief DAI spike to ~$1.30 on Coinbase, which fed the then-oracle, caused roughly $89M of liquidations on Compound; affected users were not compensated.

Past incident (29-30 Sep 2021): a bug in the Comptroller upgrade from Proposal 62 over-distributed COMP rewards (tens of millions of USD); user deposits were not at risk, but the fix needed further governance proposals (63/64) over about a week.
notes: Addresses are taken from the mainnet network config embedded in the official v2 docs (docs.compound.finance/v2 now redirects to docs.compound.xyz/v2/), which matches compound-finance/compound-protocol networks/mainnet.json; the Price Feed address is from the v2 Prices docs page and equals Comptroller.oracle() on-chain; Maximillion is from the official networks/mainnet.json. keyFunctions are listed once on cUSDC (CErc20 interface) and on cETH (payable variants); all other cTokens share the cUSDC interface (cTokens have 8 decimals). Delegator markets (proxy: true) are CErc20Delegator proxies. cWBTC (0xC11b...) is the original WBTC market and cWBTC2 (0xccF4...) the later one; both report symbol cWBTC. Left out: CompoundLens, interest-rate models, Reservoir and older Comptroller implementations (listed in mainnet.json but not needed by agents), and all Compound III (Comet) contracts, which belong to a separate protocol entry. The old api.compound.finance REST API is not listed because it is not documented as live.

offchainApis.name: Curve API
offchainApis.use: Pool lists with coins, balances, TVL, APYs and gauge data: e.g. /getPools/all/{blockchainId} (ethereum, arbitrum, base, ...), /getPoolList/{blockchainId}, /getAllGauges, /getVolumes/{blockchainId}, /getTokens/all/{blockchainId}. OpenAPI spec at https://api.curve.finance/v1/openapi.json. Use it to pick pools and coin indices for routes.

offchainApis.name: Curve Prices API
offchainApis.use: Pool metadata, OHLC, trades, volume, liquidity and LP positions, crvUSD markets: e.g. /v1/pools/{chain}/{address}, /v1/ohlc/{chain}/{address}, /v1/liquidity/{chain}/{user}/positions, /v1/crvusd/markets. OpenAPI spec at https://prices.curve.finance/feeds-docs/openapi.json.

offchainApis.name: Curve deployments JSON
offchainApis.use: Machine-readable list of every official Curve contract per chain (routers, registries, factories, gauges, tokens, crvUSD, LlamaLend).

actions.name: swap via router
actions.description: Swap any tokens through up to 5 Curve pools.
actions.how: Compute _route and _swap_params off-chain (Curve JS @curvefi/api router or curve-router-js), or for one hop: pool = MetaRegistry.find_pools_for_coins(tokenIn, tokenOut)[0]; (i, j, _) = MetaRegistry.get_coin_indices(pool, tokenIn, tokenOut); route = [tokenIn, pool, tokenOut, 0x0...]; params[0] = [i, j, 1, pool_type, n_coins]. Quote router.get_dy(route, params, amount); approve tokenIn to the router (Ethereum v1.2 0x45312ea0eFf7E09C83CBE249fa1d7598c4C8cd4e); router.exchange(route, params, amount, minOut).

actions.name: swap directly in a pool
actions.description: Single-pool swap without the router.
actions.how: Find indices with pool.coins(n) or MetaRegistry.get_coin_indices; approve coin i to the pool; pool.exchange(i, j, dx, min_dy). Stableswap pools use int128 indices, Twocrypto/Tricrypto-NG use uint256.

actions.name: add liquidity
actions.description: Deposit coins into a pool for LP.
actions.how: Approve each coin to the pool; quote calc_token_amount(amounts, true); add_liquidity(amounts, minLP). Amount array length = n_coins (NG stableswap takes a dynamic array). Remove with remove_liquidity_one_coin(lp, i, min) after calc_withdraw_one_coin.

actions.name: stake LP for CRV
actions.description: Earn CRV emissions on Ethereum.
actions.how: gauge = MetaRegistry.get_gauge(pool); approve LP to gauge; gauge.deposit(amount). Claim CRV with Minter.mint(gauge); extra rewards with gauge.claim_rewards() on newer gauges.

actions.name: lock CRV (veCRV)
actions.description: Get voting power, boost and revenue.
actions.how: CRV.approve(veCRV, amt); veCRV.create_lock(amt, unlockTime up to now+4y). Vote with GaugeController.vote_for_gauge_weights(gauge, bps). Claim weekly crvUSD revenue with FeeDistributor.claim(). Withdraw only after expiry: veCRV.withdraw().

actions.name: save in scrvUSD
actions.description: Earn the crvUSD savings rate.
actions.how: crvUSD.approve(scrvUSD, amt); scrvUSD.deposit(amt, receiver); exit with redeem(shares, receiver, owner).

risks: July 30, 2023: a Vyper compiler bug (versions 0.2.15, 0.2.16, 0.3.0 had broken @nonreentrant locks) let attackers re-enter and drain several Curve pools compiled with those versions (tens of millions of USD lost; partly recovered). Current pool implementations use fixed compiler versions, but old pools and other Vyper contracts may still carry legacy code risk.
Depeg risk: in stable pools an LP ends up holding mostly the depegged asset if one coin loses its peg; losses can be permanent.

Permissionless factories: anyone can deploy pools with any token (including malicious or fee-on-transfer tokens). Only use pools whose coins you have verified; MetaRegistry/API listing is not an endorsement.
Volatile (Twocrypto/Tricrypto) pools have impermanent loss and re-pegging dynamics; quotes for multi-hop routes can move between quote and execution: always set _expected/min_dy.

Governance: the Curve DAO (veCRV) controls pool parameters, gauge additions and crvUSD markets; the Emergency DAO (5-of-9 multisig) can kill gauges and cancel parameter changes. The AddressProvider is administered by a Curve individual and its IDs can change, so verify addresses it returns.
veCRV locks cannot be withdrawn before expiry and are non-transferable. crvUSD loans in LLAMMA are soft-liquidated gradually and can be hard-liquidated if health drops below 0.
USDT (3pool coin 2) requires approve(0) before changing a non-zero allowance; 3pool's exchange returns no value.
notes: All addresses come from Curve's official deployments data (docs.curve.finance/deployments.json, rendered at docs.curve.finance/developer/deployments.md), except the 3pool/3Crv/3pool gauge (official curvefi/curve-contract GitHub README and pooldata.json) and the crvUSD/USDC pool (example pool in the official CurveRouterNG docs). Every Ethereum address and every L2 router/AddressProvider/MetaRegistry was checked for code on-chain; router versions were read on-chain (Ethereum 0x45312ea0... = 1.2.0, 0x16C6521D... = 1.1.0, all listed L2 routers = 1.1.0). Wiring checked: MetaRegistry.get_pool_from_lp_token(3Crv) = 3pool, get_gauge(3pool) = the listed gauge, scrvUSD.asset = crvUSD, ControllerFactory.stablecoin = crvUSD, crvUSD/USDC pool coins = [USDC, crvUSD]; the Ethereum AddressProvider IDs were enumerated on-chain. Signatures are from Sourcify-verified Vyper sources (router v1.2, MetaRegistry, factories, veCRV, GaugeController, Minter, FeeDistributor, ControllerFactory, 3pool, gauge, scrvUSD's Yearn V3 implementation, crvUSD/USDC pool implementation) and Curve docs (AddressProvider ABI, NG pool and LiquidityGaugeV6 signatures). Pools are not enumerated here: discover them with MetaRegistry.find_pools_for_coins / pool_list, the factories' pool_list, or the Curve API. CRV emissions are claimed via the Minter only on Ethereum; L2 gauges are child gauges (see docs.curve.finance/developer/gauges/xchain-gauges/). Not listed: L2 factories, CRV/crvUSD/scrvUSD token addresses on L2s and the ~25 other chains (all in deployments.json), LlamaLend v1/v2 contracts (separate DefiLlama entries), individual crvUSD controllers (get them from ControllerFactory), calc zaps, fee burners and DAO Aragon voting contracts. The AddressProvider ID 2 'Exchange Router' on Ethereum still points to router v1.1 while the deployments page also lists v1.2; both work with the same route encoding.

name: EigenLayer (EigenCloud)
description: EigenLayer restaking on Ethereum: deposit LSTs (stETH, rETH, cbETH, ...) or EIGEN into strategies via the StrategyManager, delegate to an operator through the DelegationManager, withdraw through a ~14-day queue, and claim AVS rewards with merkle proofs from the RewardsCoordinator. Native ETH restaking goes through EigenPods. Restaked assets are slashable.

keyFunctions.description: Deposit ERC-20 into a strategy: (strategy, token, amount in token base units). Approve the StrategyManager (not the strategy) for the token first. Credits deposit shares to msg.sender; if msg.sender is delegated, the shares are delegated to that operator too. Strategy must be whitelisted (strategyIsWhitelistedForDeposit). Returns depositShares.
Deposit on behalf of a staker with their EIP-712 signature: (strategy, token, amount, staker, expiry, signature). Caller pays the tokens.
Deposit shares of (staker, strategy). Deposit shares are not reduced by slashing; use DelegationManager.getWithdrawableShares for the withdrawable amount.
Returns (address[] strategies, uint256[] depositShares) for a staker (ERC-20 strategies only; native ETH shares live in EigenPodManager).
Number of strategies a staker has deposits in (max 32).
True if deposits into the strategy are allowed.
Pause bitmap; non-zero bits mean some actions are paused (0 on 2026-11-25).

Delegate ALL of msg.sender's restaked assets to an operator: (operator, approverSignatureAndExpiry=(bytes signature, uint256 expiry), approverSalt). If delegationApprover(operator) is the zero address, pass an empty signature ("0x", 0) and salt 0x00..00; otherwise you need an EIP-712 signature from the approver (digest from calculateDelegationApprovalDigestHash) with an unused salt. Reverts if already delegated or the operator is not registered. A staker can be delegated to one operator only.

Undelegate a staker (callable by the staker, or by the operator / its approver to force-undelegate). Queues withdrawals for ALL the staker's shares (one withdrawal per strategy) and returns their withdrawal roots; these must be completed after the delay like any withdrawal. Operators cannot undelegate.

Undelegate (queuing withdrawals for all shares) and delegate to a new operator in one call. Queued shares can later be completed as shares (receiveAsTokens=false) to restake them with the new operator.

Queue withdrawals. Each QueuedWithdrawalParams = (address[] strategies, uint256[] depositShares, address __deprecated_withdrawer). depositShares are deposit shares (see StrategyManager.getDeposits / getDepositedShares), not tokens; the withdrawer field is ignored (only the staker can complete). Returns withdrawal roots. Shares stay slashable for MIN_WITHDRAWAL_DELAY_BLOCKS.

Complete one withdrawal after minWithdrawalDelayBlocks() (100800 blocks, ~14 days) have passed since startBlock: (Withdrawal = (address staker, address delegatedTo, address withdrawer, uint256 nonce, uint32 startBlock, address[] strategies, uint256[] scaledShares) exactly as queued, tokens[] = each strategy's underlyingToken() in the same order (any value for beacon-chain ETH), receiveAsTokens). receiveAsTokens=true sends tokens to the staker; false re-credits shares (delegated to the current operator). Amount received is reduced by any slashing up to the completion block. Only the staker can call. Get the struct from getQueuedWithdrawals(staker) or the SlashingWithdrawalQueued event.
Batch version of completeQueuedWithdrawal.
Returns (Withdrawal[] withdrawals, uint256[][] shares) for a staker: the structs to pass to completeQueuedWithdrawal and the shares currently expected (after slashing).
Returns (Withdrawal, uint256[] shares) for a withdrawal root.
Returns (withdrawableShares[], depositShares[]) for (staker, strategies): withdrawable reflects slashing; use it to size queueWithdrawals.
Returns (strategies[], depositShares[]) across StrategyManager and EigenPodManager (includes beacon chain ETH strategy 0xbeaC0eeEeeeeEEeEeEEEEeeEEeEeeeEeeEEBEaC0).
Operator a staker is delegated to (zero address if none).
True if the staker is delegated.
True if the address is a registered operator.
Operator's delegation approver; zero address means anyone can delegate with an empty signature.
Withdrawal delay in blocks (100800 = ~14 days on mainnet, read 2026-11-25).
Hash of a Withdrawal struct; pendingWithdrawals(root) tells if it is still queued.

Claim rewards: (RewardsMerkleClaim claim, recipient). claim = (uint32 rootIndex, uint32 earnerIndex, bytes earnerTreeProof, (address earner, bytes32 earnerTokenRoot) earnerLeaf, uint32[] tokenIndices, bytes[] tokenTreeProofs, (address token, uint256 cumulativeEarnings)[] tokenLeaves). Proofs are generated off-chain from the posted distribution (EigenLayer app or the official eigenlayer CLI). Pays cumulativeEarnings minus cumulativeClaimed per token. Caller must be the earner or its claimerFor.

Let another address claim (and choose the recipient of) msg.sender's rewards.

Pick the strategy whose underlyingToken() is the token (list above, or StrategyFactory.deployedStrategies(token) for other ERC-20s). Check strategyIsWhitelistedForDeposit and getTVLLimits first. Deposits earn rewards only once delegated to an operator.
